messages.author: eadcd18168e0478f
messages.subject: Initialization of a and d
parts:
Hello Phil,
I just started to use the package and I was wondering how the initialization of a and d are done, before the EM procedure starts. It would be great to have some more information about that. Also I was reading here https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/mirt-package/theta_lim%7Csort:relevance/mirt-package/Jy4h-7-XsAo/wj-Dq5YvP_kJ that it was not possible to reduce the range of the theta during the evaluation: did you implement this option in the end?

Looking forward to hear from you.
Best,
Matteo

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Initialization of a and d
parts:
You can either supply some syntax via a mirt.model definition, or edit
the data.frame of starting values by obtaining and editing the pars =
'values' input.

RE: your second question, yes there is a theta_lim argument now.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Initialization of a and d
parts:
You need to use the START argument. If you want them fixed at these
values throughout the estimation, use FIXED as well.

theta_lim should be passed to plot() to change the default range.
You'll have to see the documentation of this generic (it's a bit
buried in R's helpfile system, but it's there if you navigate the
index).

Phil

If I run mirt(data,1) there should be an authomatic initialization, that could impact the EM performance: how that automatic initialization is done? If I set the plot limits, this doesnt mean that the limit during the EM (or monte carlo or whatever else I am using) is actually reduced right? The estimation will be always on c(-6,6), but plotting on c(-3,3) could lead in losing some info on the way? 

-M-
